description: The structured production-analysis draft an AI reasoning host produces from a user script (CF-WO-P1-004, Task B). It is the Layer A analysis contract: narrative breakdown, character resolution, emotional progression, pacing, shot and sound direction, and the open questions that need a user decision. It is a DRAFT until the production orchestrator validates it: the runtime never performs creative analysis, it only checks that the analysis is complete, that every material decision carries a provenance label, and that the user's dialogue and story are preserved. Provenance labels: EXPLICIT_FROM_USER (the user said it), FROM_APPROVED_PROJECT_CANON (an approved project record says it), INFERRED_FOR_PRODUCTION (the host inferred it for production; never presented as fact), NEEDS_USER_DECISION (unresolved and material; the job must ask). This schema carries no timestamps, so a canonical-JSON hash of it is deterministic.

character_resolutions.description: How every character in the script is resolved: an approved registered identity, a task-local design proposal, or a decision the user must make. An approved identity always wins; a proposal never registers anything permanently.

character_ref.description: How the script refers to this character (name or description as written in the script).

proposal_id.description: The character-design proposal id, required when resolution is task-local-proposal.

provenance_note.description: One line saying why this provenance label applies (for example which approved record, or what was inferred).

registered_character_id.description: The approved registered character id, required when resolution is approved.

resolution.description: approved: an existing approved identity is reused. task-local-proposal: a design proposal exists for this job only. needs-decision: the user must decide.

role.description: The character's story role (for example protagonist, antagonist, supporting, narrator).

cast_class.description: How this identity appears in the production (CF-WO-P1-004-R1-ADDENDUM-IDENTITY, Task D). VISIBLE_CHARACTER: appears on screen. OFF_SCREEN_SPEAKER: speaks but never appears. NARRATOR_OR_VOICE_OVER: narration only. MENTIONED_ONLY: named but never seen or heard. The runtime recomputes this classification from the bundle; a present value that disagrees with the computed one fails the compile.

scene_ids.description: Scene ids this character participates in (CF-WO-P1-004-R1-ADDENDUM-IDENTITY, Task M: scene-specific participation). When present, the character must not be compiled into image/video packets for scenes outside this list.

dialogue_preservation.description: Proof that the analysis preserved the user's dialogue: counts must match the source ScriptContract, and no rewrite is claimed unless explicitly authorised.

mapped_line_count.description: Dialogue lines the analysis maps to performance lines. Must equal source_dialogue_line_count unless a rewrite was explicitly authorised and the originals are preserved.

notes.description: Anything the host wants to record about dialogue handling.

rewrite_requested.description: True only when the user explicitly authorised a dialogue rewrite.

source_dialogue_line_count.description: Dialogue lines in the source ScriptContract.

emotional_progression.description: The emotional arc across the story beats, in order. Each beat names the emotion and its intensity; the host must not apply the same generic expression to every character.

beat_id.description: The story beat this emotional state belongs to.

emotion.description: The emotion at this beat (for example happiness, sadness, shock, anger, fear, awe).

intensity.description: Emotional intensity from 0 to 10, matching the scene-plan and performance-plan convention.

progression_note.description: How this beat follows from the previous one.

provenance.description: Where this emotional reading came from.

format_profile.description: The delivery profile this analysis was produced for. When present, the orchestrator checks it matches the production job's format profile.

chapters.description: Chapter or sequence structure for long-form work. Each chapter names the scenes it contains.

delivery_profile.description: Short-form and long-form share the same contracts and orchestration; only the profile differs.

duration_target_seconds.description: Target total duration in seconds, when the user gave one.

id.description: Unique id of this analysis draft.

narrative_structure.description: The story's structure as analysed (for example three-act, episodic, explainer-steps, documentary-chapters).

notes.description: Anything else the host wants to record about the analysis.

open_questions.description: Unresolved details that would materially change the story, identity, rights, privacy, safety, budget or production outcome. Every entry here must carry provenance NEEDS_USER_DECISION. Ordinary missing creative details are inferred and labelled INFERRED_FOR_PRODUCTION instead — never listed here.

provenance.description: Always NEEDS_USER_DECISION for an open question.

question.description: The question to put to the user.

why_material.description: Why this detail would materially change the story or production if decided wrong.

pacing.description: Opening, ending and overall pacing as analysed.

ending.description: How the story ends (as written by the user — never a changed ending).

opening.description: How the story opens (hook or establishing beat).

provenance.description: Where the pacing reading came from.

premise.description: The story premise in one or two sentences, as analysed from the user's script.

project_id.description: The project this analysis belongs to.

scenes.description: Scene-by-scene narrative breakdown, in story order. The host identifies scene boundaries, purpose, beats, relationships, conflict, stakes, reveals and transitions — it never invents events, changes relationships or the ending, adds scenes or subplots, or removes important events.

beats.description: Dramatic beats inside the scene, in order.

character_refs.description: Characters present in this scene, by script reference.

location_brief.description: Where the scene takes place and what the location must show.

provenance.description: Where the scene breakdown came from (usually EXPLICIT_FROM_USER for the scene itself).

purpose.description: What this scene does in the story.

scene_id.description: Stable scene id, matching the Scene Plan the drafts will build.

time_of_day.description: Time of day for the scene, when the script or production needs it.

transition_to_next.description: How this scene hands over to the next one.

background_design.description: What the background must show and how it is composed. The background supports the main story action; it must not be unnecessarily busy.

weather.description: Weather for the scene, when the script or production needs it (for example clear morning, light rain, dusk haze).

atmosphere.description: Atmosphere / mood of the environment (for example quiet river calm, tense market crowd).

foreground_requirements.description: What the foreground must contain and how it frames the action.

midground_requirements.description: What the midground must contain (principal action layer, key props, secondary characters).

background_requirements.description: What the background must contain and what it must leave out, so it supports rather than overwhelms the action.

environment_continuity.description: What must stay the same as neighbouring scenes (light direction, weather state, set dressing, time progression).

asset_references.description: Approved asset references this scene depends on, by stable id. An approved existing asset always wins over an inferred proposal.

kind.description: What kind of asset this is (for example location-reference, prop-reference, character-reference, lighting-reference).

reference_id.description: The approved reference record id, when the asset is an approved record.

important_props.description: Important props in this scene, by stable prop id. Each entry is either an approved permanent prop (approved_prop_id, validated against schemas/prop.json) or a task-local proposal (design_brief). A newly inferred temporary prop must never become a permanent registered prop without authorization.

approved_prop_id.description: The approved permanent prop id (schemas/prop.json), when this prop is an approved record. Approved props are reused, never redesigned.

approved_reference_ids.description: Approved reference ids for this prop (images or records), when available.

continuity_restrictions.description: What must not change about this prop across scenes (for example same cracked handle, same position on the table).

design_brief.description: Design brief for a task-local prop proposal. Required when there is no approved_prop_id.

physical_requirements.description: Physical requirements (size, weight, material, how it is held or used).

prop_id.description: Stable prop id within this job (for example prop-lantern-001).

provenance.description: Where this prop entry came from.

provenance_note.description: One line saying why this provenance label applies.

script_contract_id.description: The id of the source ScriptContract this analysis was produced from.

shot_direction.description: Shot-level visual direction the host proposes, per shot. The runtime checks that shot ids referenced here exist in the Shot Plan drafts; it never claims a media model supports a control its capability record does not verify.

lighting_intent.description: Motivated lighting intent for the shot.

provenance.description: Where this shot direction came from.

purpose.description: What this shot does in the scene.

size.description: Shot size intent (for example wide, medium, close-up).

sound_direction.description: Sound direction per scene: what the scene needs (dialogue, ambience, foley, music, intentional silence) and why. Never forces every layer into every shot.

cue_type.description: The kind of sound this cue is.

intent.description: What this sound does in the scene.

provenance.description: Where this sound decision came from.

cue_id.description: Stable cue id within this job (for example cue-sc01-amb-001).

shot_id.description: The shot this cue belongs to, when it is shot-scoped.

beat_id.description: The story beat this cue belongs to, when it is beat-scoped.

start_anchor.description: What the cue's start is anchored to. Relative anchors are used when no exact global timecode exists; an exact global timecode is never invented.

end_anchor.description: What the cue's end is anchored to, when it has one.

start_offset_seconds.description: Seconds after the start anchor at which the cue starts, when known. Relative to the anchor, never a global timecode.

duration_seconds.description: Cue duration in seconds, when known.

distance.description: Apparent distance of the sound source (for example close, mid, distant).

perspective.description: Listening perspective for the cue (for example on-camera, off-screen, point-of-view).

intensity.description: Cue intensity from 0 to 10, matching the scene-plan and performance-plan convention.

sync_target.description: What this cue must synchronise with (for example a visible action, a dialogue line, a beat).

mixing_priority.description: Mixing priority for this cue (for example dialogue-first, foreground, background). Dialogue-first mixing is preserved: a cue never drowns the dialogue.

title: Production Analysis
